description: T10 (#13) meta panel: Gradebook grades our own build-agent sessions in this repo, applying the same recording contract (docs/conventions.md, ADR 0001/0002) the toy-world dashboard (#7) applies to simulated decisions - a third proof surface, capped at exactly one bounded panel, never a substitute for the substrate. One decision = one ticket's Claude Code build-agent session (team convention: one ticket = one branch = one PR). The reality grade is whether the ticket shipped correctly, per this repo's own definition of done (CLAUDE.md: '/spec-review passes both axes AND the full test suite is green') - a merged PR is the recorded fact that gate cleared. HONEST SCOPE (verified, not an oversight): only Mukund's own Claude Code sessions land claude_code.* telemetry in this live stack as of this ticket - Rutik's tunnel died 2026-07-19 with nothing since, Vedant/Anish have zero samples, never connected. This is Mukund's own build-agent telemetry, not yet a genuine team-fleet view. Historical tickets (recorded via dashboards/scripts/record_build_fleet_sessions.py) carry NO cost attribute: claude_code.* metrics carry no repo/project/cwd label anywhere in their schema (verified against the live attrs/scope_attrs/resource_attrs on claude_code.cost.usage), so a day's or a PR-window's cost figure would blend every project Mukund worked on, not just this repo - and this repo's PRs are frequently on stacked/concurrent branches (see PR #21: 'Stacked on 6-toy-world'), so a wall-clock-window split across tickets was tried and rejected as a guess dressed as precision. The one exception is the current ticket's own session (#13): its session.id is directly knowable, so its cost is queried from claude_code.cost.usage filtered to that exact session.id - genuinely attributable, not window-guessed. Panel shows two facts side by side rather than a blended average, exactly because averaging a known-cost subset over an all-decisions count would misrepresent the gap the same way panel-1 in #7 already documents its own numerator/denominator caveat. OPEN QUESTION FOR THE TEAM (flagged, not unilaterally resolved on #7's already-shipped dashboard): gradebook.decisions.graded / gradebook.decision.cost.usd are shared instruments (conventions doc section 10) - these build_session decisions will also be counted by #7's headline panels, which filter only on grade.source + score.label, not augmentloop.decision.type. Whether #7's panels should add an explicit decision_type != 'build_session' filter to keep the toy-world headline pure is a call for the team, not made here.
title: Gradebook Meta: Grading Our Own Build Fleet (T10, self-referential proof surface)

widgets.description: Two facts, not a blended average (see dashboard description for why): (1) how many of our own build-agent tickets shipped correctly (merged = cleared this repo's spec-review + green-tests gate), and (2) how much of that is honestly cost-attributable right now (only the current ticket's own session.id - historical tickets are correct but carry no cost, and that is intentional, not a bug; see dashboard description). Filter: augmentloop.decision.type = 'build_session' AND gen_ai.evaluation.score.label = 'correct' AND augmentloop.grade.source IN ('math','reality') - the same ADR 0001 headline rule #7 uses, scoped to our own build-fleet decision type so this never blends into the toy-world's numbers (and vice versa, modulo the open cross-cutting question noted in the dashboard description).
